headline: Volumes grow despite costly payer-mix shift
summary_short: Revenue rose 3.6% to $19.85B and adjusted EPS grew 3.7% to $7.22, while net income fell 3.9% to $1.579B. HCA repurchased $2.97B of stock and expects full-year results in the upper half of guidance.
summary_long: Same facility admissions rose 2.7% and equivalent admissions 3.0%, with ER visits up 5.1%; inpatient surgeries fell 1.4% and outpatient surgeries 3.7%. An increase in uninsured volume, mainly from lost exchange coverage, cut pre-tax income by about $400M. Operating cash flow was $4.461B and capex $1.357B. Total debt was $50.5B. The quarterly dividend was declared at $0.78 per share.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EPS and Adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP measures. GAAP EPS growth benefits from a lower share count (7.23M shares repurchased in the quarter) while net income fell. Guidance ranges were issued July 14 and are not restated in the release read.

drivers.explanation: A payer mix shift toward uninsured volume, mainly patients who lost exchange coverage, had an unfavorable pre-tax impact of roughly $400 million.
Same facility equivalent admissions grew 3.0% and revenue per equivalent admission grew 0.6%.
Net income declined but share repurchases of 7.23 million shares reduced the diluted share count.
CEO cites scale and disciplined culture despite federal policy changes and believes HCA is positioned to end the year positively.
